title: US Youth Soccer ODP Player Manual
why: A short manual written for players that turns ten principles of attacking play into simple rules you can take onto the pitch.

title: U.S. Soccer Coaching Curriculum (2011)
why: Clear, diagrammed definitions of support, width, depth, pressure, cover, balance and compactness, the same vocabulary fotbol uses in its feedback.

title: Coaches' Voice: football tactics explained
why: Diagrammed explainers on rest defence, defensive blocks, half-spaces, third-man runs and pressing.

title: The Football Analyst: football tactics explained
why: Plain-language tactics articles, including a handy list of the moments that should make a team press.

title: Soccer iQ, volumes 1 and 2 (Dan Blank)
why: Short, rule-like chapters for players on habits such as forcing an attacker onto their weaker foot and blocking the return pass.

title: England Football Learning: free courses
why: Free introductory courses from the FA that suit adults and parents, though they say little about positioning.

title: U.S. Soccer grassroots coaching pathway (4v4 to 11v11)
why: Short courses for each game format built on the same four moments of the game that fotbol uses.
note: The introduction is free; the format courses may not be.

title: Football's Principles of Play (Peter Prickett)
why: The best single book on the principles of play, with more than 90 diagrams to check your understanding against.

title: FIFA Training Centre
why: Credible practice sessions and tournament analysis, including high-block pressing, corners and goalkeeper positioning.

title: The FA England DNA: how we play out of possession
why: A clean map of the game (in possession, out of possession and the transitions) that frames defending as delay, deny and dictate.

title: Coachbetter: how the back four behaves
why: Practical rules for when a back line should step up, drop or shift, including the crescent and L shapes.

title: Soccer Coach Weekly: what is covering?
why: A clear explanation of the angle and distance the second defender should take behind the presser.

title: Minnesota Youth Soccer: defending coaching points
why: A one-page summary of what the first and second defenders should do.

title: Keeperstop: how far off the line should the goalkeeper be?
why: One of the few goalkeeping guides that gives actual distances off the line for different ball positions.

title: DFB fussball.de: Die Viererkette systematisch schulen
why: The German federation's guidance on shifting a back four while keeping the gaps even.

title: Spielverlagerung
why: Deep analysis of positional play, half-spaces and counter-pressing, plus a glossary of terms such as cover shadow and zone 14.

title: Touchline Theory: a practical guide to positional play
why: A readable guide to the five lanes, the free player and pinning defenders in place.

title: Motzenbecker: the five superiorities
why: Gives you words for the different kinds of advantage a team can create: numbers, position, quality, timing and teamwork.

title: The Outfield: let's talk about the salida lavolpiana (John Muller)
why: A precise look at when a holding midfielder should drop between the centre-backs, and why it only makes sense against two strikers.

title: Fussball-Training Trainerblog: Viererkette, Abstaende und Verschieben
why: Explains why fixed distances in metres can mislead a back four and names the shapes it can take.

title: Between the Posts
why: A steady stream of tactical match reports, useful for spotting these principles in real games.

title: Inverting the Pyramid (Jonathan Wilson, revised 2024)
why: The history of tactics, showing how back fours, zonal marking and pressing came about.

title: Zonal Marking and The Mixer (Michael Cox)
why: Readable histories of modern tactics that explain why today's teams play the way they do.

title: Breaking The Lines: tactics YouTubers to watch
why: A curated list of channels, including The Coaches' Voice, James Lawrence Allcott, Tactics HUB and RDF Tactics, that break tactics down on video.
